title: Linear vs Binary Search
topic: Why binary search finds one item in a million with only 20 checks

beats.cue: Two panels already filling with 64 sorted boxes; target number pulses gold; tick cascade
beats.text: You need one number hiding in a sorted list. Watch two strategies race to find it.

beats.cue: Top: linear cursor steps box by box. Bottom: binary probes the middle, too high / too low callouts
beats.text: Up top, linear search checks every box, one by one. Down below, binary search jumps to the middle and asks one question: too high, or too low?

beats.cue: Half of the bottom boxes dim each probe; binary FOUND at 6 checks while linear is still crawling
beats.text: Each answer throws away half of what's left. Sixty-four boxes? Binary needs six guesses. Linear might need sixty-four.

beats.cue: Boxes shatter into a million-pixel data wall; linear counter races to 1,000,000, binary steps to 20
beats.text: Now scale it to a million items. Linear search could grind through a million checks. Binary search? Done in twenty.

beats.cue: Scoreboard rows 1K -> 10, 1M -> 20, 1B -> 30, then HALVE IT stamp
beats.text: That's the power of halving. Double the data, and you pay just one extra step. Sort first, then search smart.
